column1: # CI budgets (#1437). The only place a number is typed: `ci_budget_report.sh` reads this file
# and compares it with a run's own jobs, and the verdict is its exit status.
#   stage <TAB> budget_minutes <TAB> set_at <TAB> set_from
# `set_from` is the measurement the number came from, quoted with its run id. A budget without
# one cannot be compared to the number it should be, so it is not a check — the report fails on
# the row rather than on the run.
# **A budget is set from the worst run measured so far, rounded up.** Not from the mean: two runs
# of one workflow differ by 0.4-1.3 minutes per stage, so a budget set to the best observation
# fires on noise and is ignored within a week. A breach then means one thing: slower than
# anything measured.
# The ratchet has two halves, both enforced by `ci_budget_report.sh --base <ref>`: a budget may
# be **lowered** after a win (that is the point), may **not be raised** unless `set_from` changes
# too, and a row may not be deleted.
# ## The rows below are the post-children-2-4 workflow
# **Measured, run 42388558670 (`3eafc20b`, warm cache, nothing narrowed): 12.4 min wall,
# 49.5 job-minutes over 24 jobs.** The epic's targets were <= 22 min wall and <= 70
# job-minutes; from 43.5 / 159.4 the pipeline now costs 12.4 / 49.5 in the case that runs
# *everything*. The ceilings stay at the cold-cache worst case (23 / 115), because that is what
# a refused restore costs, and a ceiling that only holds when the cache hits is not a ceiling.
# **Measured, run 42388558670 (`3eafc20b`, warm cache, nothing narrowed): 12.4 min wall,
# 49.5 job-minutes over 24 jobs.** The epic's targets were ≤ 22 min wall and ≤ 70 job-minutes;
# from 43.5 / 159.4 the pipeline now costs 12.4 / 49.5 in the case that runs *everything*.
# The ceilings stay at the cold-cache worst case (23 / 115) because that is what a refused
# restore costs, and a ceiling that only holds when the cache hits is not a ceiling.
# Set from run 42373245654 (`9105cf8b`) — the first run with no `build` job (#1438), one shared
# cache (#1439) and the suite partitioned (#1440) — and that run was **cold**: the shared cache
# key had never been written. The baseline it replaced, for the record:
#   wall            43.5 / 44.7 min           22.7 min
#   jobs                   29                 23
#   integration     14.9 / 15.6 min            7.8 min
# A budget is now "slower than the post-change baseline", which is what makes it a regression
# signal rather than a description of the old workflow. The epic's targets (#1436) remain
# ≤ 22 min wall and ≤ 70 job-minutes; children 3-5 land the wall figure, the job-minutes need
# the warm cache and the narrowing (#1441's second half).
